title: Payment Timeout: Did the Customer Already Pay?
businessContext: A payment provider accepts a capture but the response times out at the gateway. The checkout service retries with a new idempotency key, and delayed webhooks arrive after customers have retried checkout.
problemStatement: Customers report two card debits for one order while checkout displays "payment failed". Work through three timed developments, justify your actions, and write an evidence-based incident response. The simulation starts paused; advancing time can expire unanswered decisions.
constraints: A network timeout is not proof that a payment failed.
Do not blindly refund or repeat all captures.
Retain provider operation IDs and an audit trail for reconciliation.
All telemetry is synthetic. Actions only affect this practice simulation.
candidateTasks: Contain customer impact while preserving evidence and data integrity.
Respond to each new development and explain the selected action.
Cite telemetry supporting the root cause; distinguish observation from inference.
Define a permanent correction, regression coverage, recovery gates, and stakeholder update.

hints: cap_17 succeeded before the gateway timeout for order 771.
Disable blind capture retries for uncertain operations; display pending status and keep original keys and provider IDs.
Persist one logical operation key before the first provider call and reuse it only with the same payload on retries.
alternativeApproaches: Use a provider PaymentIntent-like lifecycle with one durable intent per logical checkout and authoritative state retrieval.
Serialize payment work through an outbox-backed worker, while retaining idempotent provider calls and reconciliation.
commonMistakes: Assuming a timeout proves no side effect occurred.
Generating idempotency keys inside retry loops.
Treating webhook arrival order as authoritative or refunding unverified captures.
